answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is stake-weighted identity bonding. Each agent must lock part of its balance as a bond before it can attest, grade, or claim rewards. One operator spinning up thousands of fake agents then has to lock proportionally more capital per identity, so the cost of a sybil swarm grows with its size. Peers can also check how long each bond has existed. Like a reef or a grove, honest participation builds up slowly, which makes sudden swarms stand out. Reputation should climb a trellis of past verified work rather than one-off claims.
